lit.\u0027¿Cuántos gramos de NaCl (58,44 g/m: "How many grams of NaCl (58.44 g/mol) are there in 500 mL of 0.20 M solution?"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eAl diluir se añade di:
"

When diluting, solvent is added and the moles of solute do not change: C₁V₁ = C₂V₂. Take an aliquot V₁ of a concentrated solution C₁ and bring it to V₂: the new concentration is C₂ = C₁V₁/V₂. The number of particles is the same, but they are farther apart.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eAl mezclar dos disolu:
"

When two solutions of the same solute are mixed, the moles add and so do the volumes (approx.): C = (C₁V₁ + C₂V₂) / (V₁ + V₂). The final concentration lies between the two initial ones.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003emolar:
"

Molarity is the amount of solute per liter of solution: M = n / V. The solute is weighed, dissolved in some water and made up to the mark in a volumetric flask. Increase the mass of solute and watch the concentration rise and the color intensify.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003ePara preparar un volu:
"

To prepare a volume V at concentration M, weigh m = M · V · Mmolar grams. Example: 250 mL of 0.40 M CuSO₄ requires 0.40 × 0.250 × 159.61 = 15.96 g. The final volume is that of the flask, not of the water added.

"
